content.text:
The drawing shows a urea, N-aryl-N'-aryl, with these parts:

- **Left ring:** a benzene bearing the urea NH at C1, fluorine at C2 (ortho) and a methyl at C5 (meta to the NH, para to the F). The methyl-bearing carbon is the top-left vertex, and the ring runs C1 (NH), C2 (F), C3, C4, C5 (CH3), C6.
- **Middle ring:** a para-disubstituted benzene linking the urea NH to the indazole.
- **Right bicycle:** a 3-amino-1H-indazole attached through its C4. The pyrazole ring has C3 carrying NH2, then N2 (drawn double-bonded to C3) and N1H. The benzo ring runs C3a, C4 (aryl attached), C5, C6, C7, C7a.

SMILES for the left ring: Cc1ccc(F)c(NC(=O)N...)c1

Full SMILES: Cc1ccc(F)c(c1)NC(=O)Nc1ccc(cc1)-c1cccc2[nH]nc(N)c12

Check of the indazole: c1cccc2[nH]nc(N)c12 starts at C4 (attached to the phenyl), then C5, C6, C7, C7a (ring label 2), then N1H, N2, C3 (NH2), and C3a closes both rings. This matches the drawing.

SMILES: Cc1ccc(F)c(c1)NC(=O)Nc1ccc(cc1)-c1cccc2[nH]nc(N)c12
